staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable snapshot, so every source location below is anchored to its exact line map.

classification.classification_note: The saved MemorySanitizer sink is a branch on a poisoned checksum value at `packet_parse():2372`, but the project bug is earlier in the CASIC path: a failed `SUPERSTAR2` parse leaves a two-byte stale prefix in front of a later CASIC packet, `packet_parse()` re-reads the CASIC length from the wrong base, and the unchecked `casic_checksum()` walk then runs across uninitialized `lexer->errout` bytes copied from the harness.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42537879 (gpsd): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target FuzzPacket [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42537879
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source snapshot / staged poc
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 12-byte witness is `01 20 ba ce 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20`. `packet_parse()` first feeds the prefix `01 20` into `nextstate()`'s `SUPERSTAR2` logic: `0x01` selects `SUPERSTAR2_LEADER`, `0x20` is saved in `ctmp`, and the following `0xba` fails the complement check, so `character_pushback()` rewinds only one byte and restarts parsing at that same `0xba` without discarding the earlier two prefix bytes from `lexer->inbuffer[0..1]`. Reprocessing from the pushed-back `0xba`, the remaining 10 bytes are accepted as a zero-payload CASIC packet, so `packet_parse()` reaches `CASIC_RECOGNIZED` with `inbufptr - inbuffer == 12`. Vulnerable code then assumes the CASIC packet starts at `inbuffer[0]` and executes `data_len = getleu16(lexer->inbuffer, 2)`, which misreads the leader bytes `ba ce` as `data_len = 0xceba` (52922) instead of the real zero payload length stored at offsets 4 and 5. Because the vulnerable code lacks the later patch guard `if (inbuflen < (data_len + 10))`, it first passes that bogus length to `casic_checksum(lexer->inbuffer + 2, data_len + 4)`. `casic_checksum()` then adds 4-byte words sequentially from `lexer->inbuffer + 2` for 52926 bytes, so that walk runs far past the 12-byte witness, through later `gps_lexer_t` fields including `lexer->errout`, and beyond the `inbuffer` array. `lexer->errout` was structure-copied from the harness's uninitialized `errout`, and the harness later writes only `lexer.errout.debug = 0`; those copied bytes first become causally relevant when the oversized checksum walk reaches them and contaminates `crc_computed`. Vulnerable code then performs a second unchecked far-offset read `getleu32(lexer->inbuffer, data_len + 6)` for `crc_expected`. The branch `if (crc_computed == crc_expected)` at `packet_parse():2372` is therefore the saved MemorySanitizer `use-of-uninitialized-value` sink. The staged patch resolves this exact path by inserting `if (inbuflen < (data_len + 10))` before the checksum reads, which rejects the misparsed `0xceba` length against `inbuflen == 12`.

source.description: First non-harness parser step on the vulnerable path. The first witness byte `0x01` is consumed as `SOH`, which diverts parsing into the `SUPERSTAR2` state machine instead of leaving the prefix in ordinary ground-state discard logic.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 12-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42537879/poc` with SHA-256 `37992bd9ac56fa7c09229e7c9160e56c2a261778a6fc27558f9bd4a5f1016512`, hex `0120bace0000202020202020`. This statement consumes byte 0 `0x01`; the following bytes `0x20` and `0xba` then drive the failed `SUPERSTAR2` complement check that leaves the stale two-byte prefix in front of the later CASIC parse.
source.note: The `SUPERSTAR2` state code is guarded by `#ifdef SUPERSTAR2_ENABLE` in the staged source, and the saved vulnerable run proves that the reproduced image included the packet-recognition path needed for this prefix-preserving behavior.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement materializes the attacker-controlled bogus length that drives the unsafe reads. Because the stale prefix remains at `inbuffer[0..1]`, offsets 2 and 3 are the CASIC leader bytes `0xba 0xce`, so `data_len` becomes `0xceba` (52922) instead of the real zero payload length at offsets 4 and 5.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: After the failed `SUPERSTAR2` pushback, the same exact witness bytes are still laid out as `01 20 ba ce 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20` in `lexer->inbuffer`. Re-reading offset 2 from that stale base directly converts attacker bytes `ba ce` into `data_len = 52922`.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `packet_parse()` uses the misparsed `data_len` to size the CASIC checksum read without first enforcing the later patch predicate `inbuflen < (data_len + 10)`. On the staged witness, `inbuflen` is only 12 while `data_len + 10` is 52932, so this call walks far beyond the current packet and into later `gps_lexer_t` storage, including the copied `lexer->errout` bytes that poison the checksum result.
root_cause.note: The staged `patch.diff` inserts the missing `if (inbuflen < (data_len + 10))` rejection immediately before this call and before `crc_expected = getleu32(...)`, preventing the out-of-bounds checksum reads for this exact witness.

sink.description: MemorySanitizer crash site. The branch consumes `crc_computed`, already contaminated by the unchecked `casic_checksum()` walk, while comparing it against `crc_expected` from a second unchecked far-offset read.
sink.note: The saved origin trace shows the uninitialized bytes were copied into `lexer->errout` by `lexer_init()` and originally came from the harness stack allocation of `errout`; the project bug is the earlier unchecked CASIC overread that reaches those bytes.

parser_admitted.description: After the pushed-back `0xba` is retried, the parser consumes the trailing 10 bytes as a CASIC-looking packet and enters `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`. At this point the CASIC path is admitted, but the stale prefix bytes still remain at `lexer->inbuffer[0..1]`.

evidence_limitations: The staged source snapshot is workspace commit `52a9fc9a933b9e084c3eacf759b7f1e64daf7310`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `2ab29d3034ca0c942147642a24c07332e01fb71c`; however the staged checkout is still vulnerable, reproduces the saved MSan crash, and the staged patch fixes the same `gpsd/packet.c` hunk there.

The authoritative runtime evidence is the staged default MemorySanitizer trace in `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `default_crash_trace.txt`. `reproduction_report.json` notes that a rebuilt workspace run still matched the vulnerable-crash expectation but lost MSan fidelity and degraded to `MemorySanitizer: SEGV` in `casic_checksum`, so `cross_tool_confirmed` remains false and the saved default trace is treated as ground truth.

fine_trace.note: Project-side uninitialized-value origin. `lexer_init()` structure-copies the harness `errout` into `lexer->errout`; the harness later writes only `lexer.errout.debug = 0`, so other copied fields such as `label` and `report` remain uninitialized bytes inside the `gps_lexer_t` object. MemorySanitizer's origin stack points to this copy and back to the stack allocation of `errout` in `FuzzPacket.c:33`. These bytes do not affect the parser path until step 8 overreads into `lexer->errout`.
Source. The first witness byte `0x01` is interpreted as `SOH`, so parsing enters the `SUPERSTAR2` header path instead of immediately discarding the prefix in ground-state logic.

fine_trace.code:
ctmp = c;          // seems a dodgy way to keep state...
        lexer->state = SUPERSTAR2_ID1;
fine_trace.note: The second attacker byte `0x20` is saved in `ctmp` as the expected complement partner for the tentative `SUPERSTAR2` header, and the parser advances to the equality check on the following byte.

The third byte is `0xba`, not `0xdf`, so the complement check fails. `character_pushback()` rewinds `inbufptr` by one byte and resets the state to `GROUND_STATE`, which means the next parse retry starts again at `0xba` while the earlier bytes `0x01 0x20` still remain at `lexer->inbuffer[0..1]`.

Reprocessing from the pushed-back `0xba`, the parser consumes the remaining 10 bytes `ba ce 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20` as a zero-payload CASIC packet and enters `CASIC_RECOGNIZED`. The packet body therefore started at `inbuffer[2]`, not at `inbuffer[0]`.

After step 5, `inbufptr` is one past byte 11 of the original witness, so `inbuflen` becomes 12. That span still counts the stale prefix bytes at offsets 0 and 1 in front of the 10-byte CASIC-looking tail.

Tainted length origin. `packet_parse()` assumes the CASIC packet begins at `inbuffer[0]` and re-reads the length from offsets 2 and 3. Here those bytes are actually the CASIC leader `0xba 0xce`, so `data_len` is misparsed as `0xceba` (52922) instead of the real zero payload length stored at offsets 4 and 5.

Root-cause step. Vulnerable code uses the bogus `data_len` as a checksum span of 52926 bytes without first enforcing the later patch predicate `inbuflen < (data_len + 10)`. This is the first step that actually consumes step 1's copied bytes: `gps_lexer_t` declares `inbuffer[MAX_PACKET_LENGTH*2+1]` and then a same-sized `outbuffer` before `errout`, so with `MAX_PACKET_LENGTH == 9216` the 52926-byte walk from `lexer->inbuffer + 2` outruns the 18433-byte input buffer by more than 34 KB, necessarily crossing later object fields and reaching `lexer->errout` before leaving the object.

A second unchecked read uses the same bogus length as a 52928-byte offset from `lexer->inbuffer[0]`. Source semantics establish that `crc_expected` is fetched from memory far beyond the 12-byte witness, but the saved MSan origin is already closed by step 8's sequential checksum walk.

Sink. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` on this comparison because step 8 already poisoned `crc_computed` with bytes read past the witness, and this branch consumes that value at the exact crash line while comparing it against the far-offset `crc_expected` from step 9.

crash_stack.function: fuzzer::FuzzerDriver(int*, char***, int (*)(unsigned char const*, unsigned long))

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch inserts `if (inbuflen < (data_len + 10))` immediately before the vulnerable `casic_checksum()` and `getleu32()` reads in the CASIC path. On the staged witness this rejects `inbuflen == 12` against the misparsed `data_len + 10 == 52932` before either unchecked read executes. The same commit also tightens the analogous ALLY length check, but the reproduced sink here is the CASIC hunk.

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Partially. The MSan poison originates from the harness `errout` copied into `lexer->errout`, but it reaches the sink only because the project CASIC path misparses `data_len` and overreads into that copied region.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack collapses the intra-function helper work into `packet_parse`; the fine trace expands the vulnerability-relevant `nextstate()`, `character_pushback()`, and checksum-read transitions that occur inside that frame.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The stale two-byte prefix leaves `data_len = 0xceba` at step 7, step 8 uses that size to make `casic_checksum()` walk across `lexer->errout` and poison `crc_computed`, step 9 performs the matching unchecked far-offset fetch of `crc_expected`, and step 10 compares those values at the exact MSan crash line.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's authoritative runtime evidence is the saved default MemorySanitizer run in `sanitizer_trace.txt` / `default_crash_trace.txt`, which fed the staged `poc` to `/out/FuzzPacket` and reported `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `packet_parse` at `/src/gpsd/gpsd-3.25.1~dev/gpsd/packet.c:2372:17`. `reproduction_report.json` notes that a rebuilt workspace run still matched the vulnerable-crash expectation but degraded to a SEGV in `casic_checksum`, so the saved default trace is the runtime ground truth.

format.name: Exact staged FuzzPacket witness
format.contract: The verified trigger is only the exact 12-byte file staged at `gt_results/arvo_42537879/poc` with SHA-256 `37992bd9ac56fa7c09229e7c9160e56c2a261778a6fc27558f9bd4a5f1016512`, hex `0120bace0000202020202020`. Its trigger semantics are precisely this prefix-preserving parser interaction: bytes `01 20` enter the `SUPERSTAR2` state machine, byte `ba` fails the complement check and is pushed back without discarding the stale prefix, and the trailing ten bytes `ba ce 00 00 20 20 20 20 20 20` are then re-read as a zero-payload CASIC packet while `inbuffer[0..1]` still hold the prefix. The staged artifacts do not justify a broader class of prefixes, CASIC packets, or arbitrary `SUPERSTAR2`/`CASIC` mixtures.
